Provenance of rgb-oddwidth.pcx

Written by this package's own encoder from a 21x7 *image.RGBA gradient, so unlike
gray8.pcx and rgba8.pcx it is not independent evidence of anything -- its only job is
to reach a scanline layout no other fixture reaches.

What it covers:

  21 pixels of truecolor need 21 bytes per plane, which the format rounds up to an even
  BytesPerLine of 22. That padding byte is decoded and discarded inside decodeRGB and
  emitted by truecolorEncoder's per-row flush. It is the only 8bpp multi-plane fixture
  where BytesPerLine exceeds the width.

  It replaced marbles.pcx (1419x1001, 3.8 MB), which was the only real-world file with
  an odd truecolor width and was a third of this directory's size on its own. The
  pixel content of marbles.pcx was never asserted on -- TestDecoder only requires that
  decoding does not error, and TestEncoder only requires a round trip -- so a 547-byte
  file covers exactly the same code.

Expected decoder behavior:

  rgb-oddwidth.pcx -> *image.RGBA, opaque, 8bpp / 3 planes, BytesPerLine 22

The gradient carries a per-pixel wobble in the blue channel so the three planes differ
and the RLE runs stay short, exercising literal bytes as well as runs.
